get_pages.name: What the pads mean
get_pages.description: Return every page and what is on each of its sixteen pads, resolved as it stands right now. Nothing is written on this device, and a room page fills itself from whatever is in the room, so this is the only way to find out what a pad will do without walking over and pressing it.

init.title: What things look like
init.description:
A colour for each kind of thing, the same in every room.

A pad shows its colour when the thing behind it is on, and white when it is off. That is the one rule the grid cannot bend, so white is not on offer.

Purple is safe only on scenes. Scenes have no on and off, so they never show white, and purple is the one colour that is hard to tell from it.

user.title: Add a page
user.description:
A page is one screen of sixteen pads. Give it a room and it fills itself from what is in that room; give it a label and it fills itself from whatever carries that label, across rooms; give it neither and it is yours to fill pad by pad.

The colour names it on the first screen, and it is the curtain that sweeps across when you go in and out.

reconfigure.title: Change this page
reconfigure.description:
A page is one screen of sixteen pads. Give it a room and it fills itself from what is in that room; give it a label and it fills itself from whatever carries that label, across rooms; give it neither and it is yours to fill pad by pad.

The colour names it on the first screen, and it is the curtain that sweeps across when you go in and out.

pads.title: Pin things to pads
pads.description:
Sixteen pads, counted the way you read them:

```
{grid}
```

The fields below are filled in with **what this page shows right now**, so you can see it and change any of it. Only what you actually change is stored: leave one as it is and that pad carries on filling itself from the page's room or label, so looking at a page and saving it does not quietly freeze it.

Clear a field and the pad goes back to being filled from the room. On a page with no room at all, these are the whole page.

What a pad *does* still comes from what is behind it — a lamp toggles, a scene runs, and holding anything a knob can adjust points the knobs at it.

A pad may also be a **readout**. Pin a door sensor or a person and it shows you rather than offering you: its colour when the door is open or the person is in, white when not, and a shudder if you press it. What is never offered is anything the grid cannot show — a temperature has no on and no off, and a pad that sat white forever would be lying about it.

error.one_source: A page fills itself from one place. Choose a room or a label, not both.
